[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the **bracket** first: (34 + 26) = 60.

Combine **positive terms**: 88 + 42 + 71 + 37 = 238.

Combine **negative terms**: 60 + 59 = 119.

Subtract the totals: 238 − 119 = 119.

**∴ The correct answer is 119.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 88 + 42 − (34 + 26) + 71 − 59 + 37

**Method:** Follow the **BODMAS** rule to solve the expression step-by-step.

⇒ 88 + 42 − **60** + 71 − 59 + 37

⇒ 130 − 60 + 71 − 59 + 37

⇒ 70 + 71 − 59 + 37

⇒ 141 − 59 + 37

⇒ 82 + 37

⇒ **119**

**∴ The correct answer is 119.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

VBODMAS Rule

The priority of operations is **Vinculum**, **Bracket**, **Of**, **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

Sign Rules

When a **minus sign** is outside a bracket, the signs of all terms inside the bracket change upon opening; however, in this case, the sum is performed inside the bracket first.

Calculation Tip

To avoid errors in long chains, always sum **positive** and **negative** values separately before the final subtraction.

questions.question: 64 + 29 of 2 - 19 + (42 ÷ 6) + 35 - 18 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve using the **VBODMAS** rule priorities: First **Bracket** (42 ÷ 6) = 7, then **Of** (29 × 2) = 58.

The expression becomes: 64 + 58 − 19 + 7 + 35 − 18.

Group positive terms: 64 + 58 + 7 + 35 = 164.

Group negative terms: 19 + 18 = 37.

Calculate the difference: 164 − 37 = 127.

**∴ The correct answer is 127.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 64 + 29 of 2 − 19 + (42 ÷ 6) + 35 − 18

**Formula Used:**

The **BODMAS** rule defines the order of operations: **B**rackets, **O**f, **D**ivision, **M**ultiplication, **A**ddition, and **S**ubtraction.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 64 + 29 of 2 − 19 + 7 + 35 − 18 (Solving **Bracket**: 42 ÷ 6) ⇒ 64 + 58 − 19 + 7 + 35 − 18 (Solving **Of**: 29 × 2) ⇒ 122 − 19 + 7 + 35 − 18 ⇒ 103 + 7 + 35 − 18 ⇒ 110 + 35 − 18 ⇒ 145 − 18 ⇒ 127

**∴ The correct answer is 127.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Order

Always follow the strict hierarchy: **Brackets** → **Of** → **Division** → **Multiplication** → **Addition** → **Subtraction**.

The 'Of' Operator

The term **'of'** acts as a multiplication but must be evaluated before any division or standard multiplication in the expression.

Addition and Subtraction Priority

Addition and subtraction have the **same level of precedence** and are generally solved from left to right, or by grouping all positive and negative terms separately.

questions.question: (8(2.5)³-1)/((6)²-5)=?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Combine 8 and (2.5)³ as (2 × 2.5)³ = 5³ = 125.

Numerator = 125 − 1 = 124.

Denominator = 36 − 5 = 31.

Division: 124 ÷ 31 = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The expression (8(2.5)³ − 1) ÷ (6² − 5)

Applying the **BODMAS** rule for **simplification**:

⇒ First, calculate the **Cube**: (2.5)³ = 2.5 × 2.5 × 2.5 = 15.625

⇒ Numerator calculation: (8 × 15.625) − 1 = 125 − 1 = 124

⇒ Denominator calculation: (6²) − 5 = 36 − 5 = 31

⇒ Final division: 124 ÷ 31 = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the order of operations: Brackets, Orders (Powers/Roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Laws of Exponents

The rule aⁿ × bⁿ = (a × b)ⁿ is useful for simplifying expressions like 2³ × (2.5)³ = (2 × 2.5)³.

Important Cubes

Memorizing cubes like 1³=1, 2³=8, 3³=27, 4³=64, and 5³=125 helps in fast calculation.

questions.question: If X=sqrt{289}times sqrt{225}times sqrt{144}, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Directly calculate the **square roots** of the known **perfect squares**: √289 = 17, √225 = 15, and √144 = 12.

Multiply the simplified values: X = 17 × 15 × 12.

Rearrange for easier calculation: X = 17 × (15 × 12) = 17 × 180 = 3060.

**∴ The correct answer is 3060.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The equation is **X** = √289 × √225 × √144.

**Formula Used:**

The value of a **square root** √n is the number which, when multiplied by itself, equals n.

**Calculations:**

⇒ X = √(17²) × √(15²) × √(12²)

⇒ X = 17 × 15 × 12

⇒ X = 255 × 12

⇒ X = 3060

**∴ The correct answer is 3060.**

**__Additional Information__**

Perfect Squares Table

Memorizing **perfect squares** from 1 to 25 (e.g., 11²=121, 12²=144, 15²=225, 17²=289) helps solve **simplification** questions rapidly.

Product Property of Square Roots

The property √a × √b = √(a × b) can also be used to simplify products under a single **radical sign** if needed.

BODMAS Rule

In mathematical expressions, always calculate **Orders** (roots and powers) before performing **multiplication** or **addition**.</p

questions.question: frac{(sqrt{8}+sqrt{2})²+(sqrt{8}-sqrt{2})²}{12sqrt{10}}=?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **algebraic identity**: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)

Here, a = √8 and b = √2

⇒ Numerator = 2(√8² + √2²) = 2(8 + 2) = 20

⇒ Value = 20 ÷ 12√10 = 5 ÷ 3√10

⇒ Result = (5 × √10) ÷ (3 × 10) = √10/6

**∴ The correct answer is √10/6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Expression = [(√8 + √2)² + (√8 − √2)²] ÷ 12√10

**Method Used:** Standard simplification of **surds** and **rationalization**.

⇒ √8 can be written as √(4 × 2) = 2√2

⇒ First term: (√8 + √2)² = (2√2 + √2)² = (3√2)² = 18

⇒ Second term: (√8 − √2)² = (2√2 − √2)² = (√2)² = 2

⇒ Numerator = 18 + 2 = 20

⇒ Expression = 20 ÷ 12√10 = 5 ÷ 3√10

⇒ To **rationalize**, multiply the numerator and denominator by √10:

⇒ (5 × √10) ÷ (3 × √10 × √10) = 5√10 ÷ 30 = √10/6

**∴ The correct answer is √10/6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities for Squares

(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²) and (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.

Rationalizing the Denominator

To remove a radical from the denominator of a fraction like x/√y, multiply both the numerator and denominator by √y.

Simplifying Radicals

A radical expression is in simplest form when the radicand has no perfect square factors other than 1, such as √8 = 2√2.

questions.question: The side of a square is 40 cm. What is the diagonal (in cm) of the square?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Side** of the square (a) = 40 cm.

**Diagonal** of a square = a√2.

Diagonal = 40 × √2 = 40√2 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 40√2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Side** of the square = 40 cm.

**Formula Used:**

In a square, the **diagonal** forms a right-angled triangle with two adjacent sides. By **Pythagoras Theorem**:

Diagonal² = Side² + Side²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ff7ee7119ddc944e9421252446dae510af3d81436ec2a4960992b64e00b66177.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Diagonal² = 40² + 40²

⇒ Diagonal² = 1600 + 1600

⇒ Diagonal² = 3200

⇒ Diagonal = √3200

⇒ Diagonal = √(1600 × 2)

⇒ Diagonal = 40√2 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 40√2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Square

Area can be calculated as Side² or (Diagonal² ÷ 2).

Perimeter of a Square

The total boundary length is given by 4 × Side.

Inradius and Circumradius

Inradius (r) = Side ÷ 2 and Circumradius (R) = Diagonal ÷ 2.

questions.question: The perimeter of a square is 28 cm. What is the area (in square cm) of the square?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Area** of a square in terms of **Perimeter** is given by: **Area = (Perimeter ÷ 4)²**

⇒ Area = (28 ÷ 4)²

⇒ Area = 7² = 49 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 49 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of the **Square** = 28 cm

**Formula used:**

Perimeter = 4 × side (a)

Area = side² (a²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/306fdb7343b72ae8676c83ffb599f1bbaae7cadbbc7d2e09129b4777568553bb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 4 × a = 28

⇒ a = 28 ÷ 4

⇒ a = 7 cm

⇒ Area = 7 × 7

⇒ Area = 49 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 49 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Diagonal of a Square

The length of the diagonal of a square with side 'a' is calculated as **a√2**.

Area in terms of Diagonal

If the diagonal 'd' is known, the area can be calculated directly using the formula **Area = d² ÷ 2**.

Inradius and Circumradius

For a square of side 'a', the **Inradius (r) = a ÷ 2** and the **Circumradius (R) = a ÷ √2**.

questions.question: Which of the following number is divisible by both 3 and 4?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check **divisibility by 4** first: The last two digits must be divisible by 4.

Options 8123 and 8495 are **odd**, so they are not divisible by 4.

Option 9342: 42 is not divisible by 4. Option 8376: 76 ÷ 4 = 19 (Yes).

Check **divisibility by 3** for 8376: Sum of digits = 8 + 3 + 7 + 6 = 24. Since 24 is divisible by 3, 8376 is the answer.

**∴ The correct answer is 8376.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers 8376, 8123, 8495, 9342.

**Formula Used:**

1. **Divisibility by 4:** Last two digits of the number must be divisible by 4.

2. **Divisibility by 3:** Sum of the digits of the number must be divisible by 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f126ce465d0d0b5b48f370ee97a904e8034f93aa59547d5940b744ae0bced32c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ For 8376: Last two digits = 76.

⇒ 76 ÷ 4 = 19 (Divisible by 4).

⇒ Sum of digits = 8 + 3 + 7 + 6 = 24.

⇒ 24 ÷ 3 = 8 (Divisible by 3).

⇒ For 9342: Last two digits = 42. 42 ÷ 4 = 10.5 (Not divisible by 4).

⇒ For 8123 and 8495: Both are odd numbers, so they cannot be divisible by 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 8376.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 12

A number is divisible by 12 if and only if it is divisible by both 3 and 4 simultaneously.

Divisibility by 6

A number is divisible by 6 if it is an even number and the sum of its digits is divisible by 3 (divisible by both 2 and 3).

Divisibility by 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the last three digits of the number are divisible by 8.

questions.question: Which of the following number is divisible by both 3 and 11?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number divisible by both **3** and **11** must be divisible by **33**.

Check **3432**: Sum of digits = 3+4+3+2 = 12 (divisible by **3**).

Difference of alternate digits: (3+3) − (4+2) = 0 (divisible by **11**).

Checking other options shows none satisfy both criteria simultaneously.

**∴ The correct answer is 3432.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The numbers are 3312, 3268, 3432, and 3520.

**Divisibility Rule of 3:** The **sum of all digits** of the number must be divisible by 3.

**Divisibility Rule of 11:** The **difference** between the sum of digits at **odd positions** and the sum of digits at **even positions** must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

⇒ **3312:** Sum = 3+3+1+2 = 9 (Divisible by 3). Difference = (3+1) − (3+2) = 4 − 5 = −1 (Not divisible by 11).

⇒ **3268:** Sum = 3+2+6+8 = 19 (Not divisible by 3).

⇒ **3432:** Sum = 3+4+3+2 = 12 (Divisible by 3). Difference = (3+3) − (4+2) = 6 − 6 = 0 (Divisible by 11).

⇒ **3520:** Sum = 3+5+2+0 = 10 (Not divisible by 3).

Since **3432** is the only number that satisfies both conditions, it is divisible by both 3 and 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 3432.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 9.

Divisibility by 4

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits are divisible by 4 or are both zero.

Divisibility by 12

A number is divisible by 12 if it is divisible by both its co-prime factors 3 and 4.

questions.question: Average of 6 consecutive odd natural numbers is 40. The just previous and the just next odd natural number to these 6 odd natural numbers are also included. What will be the new average?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any set of **consecutive numbers** in an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)**, the average is the **middle point** of the sequence.

The original average of 6 numbers is **40**.

When 1 number is added **just before** and 1 number **just after** the set, the **symmetry** of the sequence around the center remains unchanged.

Because the addition is **balanced** on both ends, the **mean** does not shift.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of 6 consecutive odd natural numbers = 40.

**Formula:** Average of an AP = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1481eaaa2be4af57ad0b307a4cb6f88b406b848a81174413c8a43be67e6369f0.png] 

⇒ Let the 6 numbers be n₁, n₂, n₃, n₄, n₅, n₆.

⇒ Total Sum = Average × Count = 40 × 6 = 240.

⇒ The 6 consecutive odd numbers centered at 40 are: 35, 37, 39, 41, 43, 45.

⇒ **Just previous** odd number = 35 − 2 = 33.

⇒ **Just next** odd number = 45 + 2 = 47.

⇒ New total count = 8 numbers.

⇒ New Sum = 240 + 33 + 47 = 320.

⇒ New Average = 320 ÷ 8 = 40.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Arithmetic Progression (AP)

The average of any sequence in AP is always exactly the middle term (if n is odd) or the mean of the two middle terms (if n is even).

Symmetry in Averages

Adding or removing terms symmetrically from both ends of an AP sequence never changes the average value.

Consecutive Odd/Even Numbers

The common difference (d) between any two consecutive odd or consecutive even numbers is always 2.

questions.question: How many numbers are there from 1 to 102 which are multiples of 5?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the number of **multiples** of a number **x** in the range **1 to n**, simply divide **n** by **x** and consider only the **integer quotient**.

Number of multiples = ⌊ 102 ÷ 5 ⌋

102 ÷ 5 = 20.4

The **integer quotient** is 20.

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers range from **1 to 102**, Multiples of **5**.

**Formula Used:** n = [(l − a) ÷ d] + 1, where **l** is the last term, **a** is the first term, and **d** is the common difference.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4d43767687345b01872fdfc30cc73d3e466350bfe9e292758a9e3d398ed493b1.png] 

⇒ Multiples of 5 in the range are: 5, 10, 15, ..., 100.

⇒ This forms an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)**.

⇒ First term (a) = 5

⇒ Last term (l) = 100

⇒ Common difference (d) = 5

⇒ n = [(100 − 5) ÷ 5] + 1

⇒ n = [95 ÷ 5] + 1

⇒ n = 19 + 1

⇒ n = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Number of Multiples in a Custom Range

To find multiples of **k** between **A** and **B**, the formula is ⌊ B ÷ k ⌋ − ⌊ (A − 1) ÷ k ⌋.

Divisibility Property

Every **nth** number in a sequence of integers is a multiple of **n**.

Sum of n Multiples

The sum of the first **n** multiples of **x** is given by the AP sum formula: Sₙ = (n ÷ 2) × [First multiple + Last multiple].

questions.question: Six bells commence ringing together and ring at intervals of 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 and 24 seconds respectively. In 18 minutes, how many times do they ring together? (including the first ringing together at commencement)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the **LCM** of ringing intervals: LCM(4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24) = **240 seconds**.

Convert interval to minutes: 240 seconds ÷ 60 = **4 minutes**.

Number of rings = (Total Time ÷ LCM interval) + 1 (Commencement ring).

Number of rings = (18 ÷ 4) + 1 = 4.5 + 1 → 4 + 1 = **5 times**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

questions.question: Cost price of an article is Rs. 650. The loss percentage is 10 percent. What is the value of loss?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss is calculated as 10% of the **Cost Price**.

10% of ₹650 = 650 ÷ 10 = ₹65.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹65.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b7caa60f5007a018588e0a026c1e7c26dcea4de4fd0c4741c9489102806dff6.png] 

**Given:**

**Cost Price (CP)** of the article = ₹650

**Loss percentage** = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Loss = (Loss% × Cost Price) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Loss = (10 × 650) ÷ 100

⇒ Loss = 6500 ÷ 100

⇒ Loss = ₹65

**∴ The correct answer is ₹65.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Selling Price (SP) Calculation

In case of a loss, the **Selling Price** is always less than the **Cost Price**. SP = CP − Loss. Here, SP = 650 − 65 = ₹585.

Profit and Loss Base

Both **Profit Percentage** and **Loss Percentage** are calculated on the **Cost Price** (CP) by default. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Fractional Method

A 10% loss can be represented as 1/10. If CP is 10 units, Loss is 1 unit. 10 units = ₹650 → 1 unit = ₹65.

questions.question: A is (1/10) of B. A is how much percent less than B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **A** to **B** is **A:B = 1:10**.

The difference in parts is 10 − 1 = **9 units**.

Percentage less = (Difference / Base) × 100 = (9 / 10) × 100.

Percentage less = **90%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 90 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **A** is (1/10) of **B**.

**Formula Used:** **Percentage Less** = [(Value 1 − Value 2) / Value 1] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/42433440dda7e4d42ec356db8526a8521e347dea5444ee50f2e5b2d5db4d5632.png] 

⇒ Let the value of **B** be 100.

⇒ **A** = (1/10) × 100 = 10.

⇒ Difference between **B** and **A** = 100 − 10 = 90.

⇒ **Percentage Less** = (Difference / **B**) × 100.

⇒ **Percentage Less** = (90 / 100) × 100 = 90%.

**∴ The correct answer is 90 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Difference Formula

When comparing how much less **X** is than **Y**, the formula is: [(**Y** − **X**) / **Y**] × 100.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

Common fractions used in exams: 1/10 = 10%, 1/5 = 20%, 1/4 = 25%, 1/2 = 50%, and 9/10 = 90%.

Base of Comparison

In "**A** is how much percent less than **B**", the value following 'than' (which is **B**) is always the **denominator**.

questions.question: A person spends 20 percent of his money. He deposits 70 percent of the remaining money in the bank. If Rs. 1680 are remaining with him now, then how much money he had initially?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Remaining percentage of money = (100 − 20)% × (100 − 70)%

⇒ 80% × 30% = 24%

Given, 24% of **initial money** = Rs. 1680

⇒ 100% = (1680 ÷ 24) × 100 = 7000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 7000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Money spent = 20%

Deposit in bank = 70% of the **remaining money**

Final remaining amount = Rs. 1680

**Formula Used:**

Final Amount = Initial Amount × (1 − r₁/100) × (1 − r₂/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/71afb0c4932aa61a64772ad1bdc5770f24269c50dd3f6a3c320e50486b73bb86.png] 

Let the **initial amount** be x.

⇒ Money left after 20% spending = x × (1 − 20/100) = 0.80x

⇒ Money left after 70% bank deposit = 0.80x × (1 − 70/100)

⇒ Final remaining = 0.80x × 0.30 = 0.24x

⇒ 0.24x = 1680

⇒ x = 1680 ÷ 0.24

⇒ x = 168000 ÷ 24

⇒ x = 7000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 7000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When values are changed sequentially, the final value is Initial × (1 ± r₁/100) × (1 ± r₂/100). For spending/depositing, use the minus sign.

Effective Percentage Method

The overall remaining percentage after successive reductions of a% and b% is (100 − a) × (100 − b) / 100 percent of the original value.

Fractional Conversion

Converting percentages to fractions (e.g., 20% = 1/5, 70% = 7/10) can often simplify complex multiplication in **ratio-based** problems.

questions.question: The difference between cost price and selling price of an article is Rs. 570. Loss percentage is 25 percent. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In profit and loss, the difference between **Cost Price (CP)** and **Selling Price (SP)** represents the total **Loss**.

**Loss Percentage** = 25% = 1/4 (where 1 unit is **Loss** and 4 units is **CP**).

Given: 1 unit (Loss) = ₹570.

Therefore, 4 units (CP) = 4 × 570 = ₹2280.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2280.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference between **CP** and **SP** (Loss) = ₹570

**Loss percentage** = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Loss Percentage = (Loss ÷ Cost Price) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/192d0e9d126a50b9a8381db0f8b3b7a4b05dfddbba23745ce61909b883afd6dc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 25 = (570 ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ CP = (570 × 100) ÷ 25

⇒ CP = 570 × 4

⇒ CP = ₹2280

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2280.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage

Profit occurs when **Selling Price** is greater than **Cost Price**. Profit% = ((SP − CP) ÷ CP) × 100.

Relationship between CP and SP in Loss

When there is a **Loss**, the **Selling Price** is calculated as: SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100.

Marked Price and Discount

**Discount** is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP − Discount.

questions.question: A alone can complete 60 percent part of a work in 18 days. A alone will complete 90 percent part of the same work in how many days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the rate of work is constant, **Time** is directly proportional to the **Work Percentage**.

Ratio of work: 60% : 90% = 2 : 3

Therefore, the time ratio is also 2 : 3.

Given 2 units = **18 days**, then 1 unit = 9 days.

For **90% work** (3 units) = 3 × 9 = **27 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 27 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **A alone** for **60% work** = **18 days**.

**Formula Used:**

**Unitary Method**: Time for Required Work = (Given Time ÷ Given Work) × Required Work.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f76931bb1e7c3ef698d569a78f6b9cac1a39acfa1a137d5dd93288824090578d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken to complete **60% work** = 18 days

⇒ Time taken to complete 1% work = 18 ÷ 60 days

⇒ Time taken to complete **90% work** = (18 ÷ 60) × 90 days

⇒ Time taken = (3 ÷ 10) × 90 = 3 × 9

⇒ Time taken = **27 days**

**∴ The correct answer is 27 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportionality in Work

When efficiency is constant, the time taken is directly proportional to the amount of work: T₁ ÷ W₁ = T₂ ÷ W₂.

Calculating 100% Work Duration

To find the time for full work, divide the given days by the fraction of work completed: Total Days = Given Days ÷ (Work Percentage ÷ 100).

Rate of Work

The rate at which **A** works in this problem is 100% ÷ 30 days = 3.33% work per day or 1/30 of the total work per day.

questions.question: 3 men and 9 women together can complete a work in 18 days. A woman is twice as efficient as a man. How many men can complete this work in 14 days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency ratio of 1 **Woman** (W) to 1 **Man** (M) is 2 : 1.

Total **Men** equivalent = 3M + 9W = 3 + (9 × 2) = 21 **Men**.

Using **M₁D₁ = M₂D₂**:

21 × 18 = x × 14

x = (21 × 18) ÷ 14 = 3 × 9 = 27 **men**.

**∴ The correct answer is 27 men.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 3 **men** and 9 **women** complete work in 18 **days**. Efficiency of 1 **woman** = 2 × Efficiency of 1 **man**.

**Formula Used:** **Total Work** = **Efficiency** × **Time**

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Group (3M + 9W)
 18
 378 units
 21 units/day
 
 

 Required Men (x)
 14
 27 units/day
 
 

⇒ Let efficiency of 1 **man** = 1 unit/day.

⇒ Efficiency of 1 **woman** = 2 units/day.

⇒ Total efficiency of group = (3 × 1) + (9 × 2) = 3 + 18 = 21 units/day.

⇒ Total **work** = 21 × 18 = 378 units.

⇒ Required daily efficiency to finish in 14 **days** = 378 ÷ 14 = 27 units/day.

⇒ Since each **man** contributes 1 unit/day, **number of men** needed = 27 ÷ 1 = 27.

**∴ The correct answer is 27 men.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule Formula

For different groups working on the same task: M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂, where M is persons, D is days, H is hours, and W is work.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

**Efficiency** is inversely proportional to the **time** taken. If the efficiency ratio is a : b, then the time ratio taken to complete the same work is b : a.

Man-Days Concept

The total work can be expressed in **man-days** (number of men × number of days). It remains constant for a specific piece of work regardless of how many people are assigned.

questions.question: Speed of A and B is 12 km/hr and 30 km/hr respectively. What will be the ratio of time taken by them to complete the same distance?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **Distance** is constant, the **Ratio of Time** taken is the inverse of the **Ratio of Speed**.

Speed Ratio (A : B) = 12 : 30 = 2 : 5

Time Ratio (A : B) = Inverse of Speed Ratio = 5 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of A (SA) = 12 km/hr

Speed of B (SB) = 30 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Distance (D) = Speed × Time

Time (T) = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0754775ad309430b998cade61a055beaf5d00e70eb117bd5322a4e9eab8906f8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the constant distance be D km.

⇒ Time taken by A (TA) = D ÷ 12

⇒ Time taken by B (TB) = D ÷ 30

⇒ Ratio of time taken (TA : TB) = (D/12) : (D/30)

⇒ TA : TB = 30 : 12

⇒ Dividing both sides by 6, we get 5 : 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between Speed and Time

For a constant distance, speed is **inversely proportional** to time. S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂.

Average Speed

When two equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, the **average speed** is (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the **opposite direction**, relative speed = S₁ + S₂. In the **same direction**, relative speed = S₁ − S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: A man travelled for first 8 hours at the speed of 15 km/hr. He travelled for next 5 hours at the speed of 20 km/hr. What is his average speed (in km/hr) for the whole journey?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Apply the **Weighted Average** formula for speed: **Average Speed** = (s₁t₁ + s₂t₂) ÷ (t₁ + t₂). **Average Speed** = (15 × 8 + 20 × 5) ÷ (8 + 5) **Average Speed** = (120 + 100) ÷ 13 = 220/13 km/hr. **∴ The correct answer is 220/13 km/hr.**
